prose_updates.tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, so a queried causal transfer is governed by the compatible fiber rather than by a selected numerical root.  For odd \(m\), seeding the queried edge and closing only under graph-supported remainder monomials gives an exact terminating dependency set: separation only there identifies the transfer and yields one uniformly calibrated Wald band for the entire curve in \(C(\mathbb T;\mathbb C)\).  Prespecified finite-frequency, directed-corridor, and globally separated Wald results remain explicit corollaries.  For even \(m\), the same-law sign obstruction continues to hold on the larger unrestricted stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovations.  Exact transfer-aware certification and branch-free confidence-region inversion cover singular and nonregular cases.

project_justification.gap: Published subsampling results either use non-Gaussian shocks for positive recovery, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch.  Gong et al.'s positive theorem assumes non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions, so neither it nor the present Gaussian supplied-order result contains the other.  Prior root-recursive inference does not isolate the exact finite dependency set for one causal transfer or calibrate a simultaneous band over every unit-modulus frequency under rank-changing covariance.
project_justification.niche: A supplied causal order makes triangular divided-difference recursion available.  For the direct transfer, the sharp recursive locality is obtained by seeding \(u\to v\) and repeatedly adding only allowed off-diagonal variables that actually occur in retained \(m\)-step remainder monomials, together with their incident diagonals.  This exact closure terminates, is contained in the directed path corridor, and can be strictly smaller; its two recovered target coordinates define a smooth finite-dimensional image in \(C(\mathbb T;\mathbb C)\).
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit exact-dependency identifying map and a uniformly exact simultaneous Wald band for the full transfer curve on \(\mathbb T\), on a nonempty compact class separated only on that finite set.  The finite-frequency result with its smaller grid-specific critical value, followed by the path-corridor and globally separated conclusions, are explicit corollaries.  It also gives an unrestricted stable-Gaussian even-sign obstruction with arbitrary positive-definite innovations, plus a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with attained witnesses and finite-sample branch-free inversion.  The covariance-envelope fallback remains a validity device equal pathwise to the deterministic box, not a claimed adaptive improvement.

prose_updates.honest_scope: Positive identification and Wald inference concern stable, ordered, finite-dimensional Gaussian VAR(1) process-DAG models with known odd subsampling factor and diagonal fine innovation covariance.  Point identification and smooth recovery of \(h_{uv}\) require noncollision and derivative separation only on the exact finite \(m\)-step algebraic dependency closure seeded at \(u\to v\).  On the derivative-separated class, the Wald guarantee is simultaneous over the full unit circle; finite grids, the directed path corridor, and global separation give explicit sufficient corollaries.  Coefficients and innovation variances outside the exact closure may remain ambiguous, and no full-matrix uniqueness is claimed.  In contrast, the even-factor sign obstruction holds for every stable Gaussian VAR(1) with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance, even without a supplied order, triangularity, or graph zeros, whenever the queried coordinate is nonzero.  Outside the exact-local regular class, inference is branch-free.  No claim is made about unknown sampling factors, high-dimensional rates, VARMA or unit-root extensions, or the scientific validity of the Temperature--Ozone ordering.

prose_updates.related_work: Gong et al. (2015) motivate temporal causal recovery from subsampled data.  Their positive recovery theorem uses non-Gaussian innovations together with full-rank, nonzero-diagonal, and weak-connectivity conditions; the present positive result instead uses Gaussian innovations, a supplied order, and process-DAG restrictions, so the two positive classes are incomparable rather than related by inclusion.  Their Gaussian nonuniqueness discussion motivates the obstruction, while the present proof isolates an even-factor sign pair on the strictly larger stable Gaussian VAR(1) class with arbitrary positive-definite innovation covariance and no order or triangularity requirement.  Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019) likewise use non-Gaussian shocks and likelihood methods.  Hyttinen et al. (2017) preserve qualitative subsampling ambiguity through exact constraints, whereas the present target is a numerical rational transfer.  Smith (2003), Bini, Higham, and Meini (2005), and Higham (2008) supply triangular-root algorithms and branch theory; the new step derives the exact finite \(m\)-step graph-supported monomial dependency closure for one queried transfer and propagates its finite-dimensional Gaussian derivative into a simultaneous full-unit-circle band.  The larger directed-path corridor and global recursion remain readable corollaries.  Reiter et al. (2026) identify rational link effects from an unaliased fine-grid spectrum, and Reiter et al. (2024) derive local delta-method inference once fine-grid coefficients are differentiably estimable.  Basu and Michailidis (2015), Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012), and Giurcanu and Spokoiny (2004) provide concentration context for finite-sample moment regions.  Mixed-frequency VARMA and unit-root results of Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017), Anderson et al. (2016), and Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (2023) concern different model classes.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-dependency result still assumes a supplied scientifically defensible order and a known odd sampling factor for positive identification; it does not infer the order.  The full-frequency Wald band also requires fixed dimension, a uniform stability margin, and root-derivative and divided-difference separation on the exact closure.  The closure is exact for formal graph-supported monomial dependence in the stated triangular recursion, not a claim that every retained coefficient is numerically influential at every parameter value.  Genericity is in fine-parameter space, not observed-law image space.  Exact CAD certifies termination but not polynomial-time scalability, and executable witnesses require effective real-closed-field input.  Gong et al.'s Temperature--Ozone example is used only as a conditional \(m=2\) Gaussian ambiguity audit if external science supplies the one-way order; their fit does not establish that order, and their positive non-Gaussian theorem is not imported into this Gaussian class.
